lessonTitle: Bills of Materials and Drawing Revision

blocks.text: A pump housing is machined correctly, but the assembly line stops because the stores holds no O-ring: it was drawn in the assembly view but never listed. A bill of materials is the document that stops that happening.

blocks.markdown: An assembly drawing shows how parts fit together; it does not by itself tell purchasing or stores what to buy or make. The **bill of materials (BOM)**, also called the parts list, is a table that lists every component of the assembly exactly once, with the quantity needed per assembly. Each line has an **item number** that matches a balloon on the assembly view, so a reader can move between the picture and the list.

blocks.title: Bill of materials
blocks.text: A **bill of materials** is a structured list of all parts and standard items in an assembly. Typical columns: item number, part number or standard designation, description, quantity per assembly, and material. Fasteners and other standard parts are listed by designation, for example screw M6 x 20, not drawn separately.

blocks.markdown: A BOM is built by walking through the assembly and counting. **Identical parts share one line** with a quantity greater than 1; two different parts never share a line even if they look alike. Assemblies are conventionally listed in a consistent order, such as ascending item number, so that new items are easy to add. Subassemblies appear as one line of their own with their own BOM.

blocks.caption: A short BOM: the O-ring is a standard item listed by size, not drawn as a part

blocks.title: Building a BOM from an assembly
blocks.prompt: A pillow-block bearing assembly contains one housing, one shaft, two identical rolling bearings, four M8 x 30 bolts, four M8 nuts and eight M8 washers (a washer under each bolt head and under each nut). Produce the BOM line count and the total number of individual pieces.

steps.text: List one line for each distinct part or standard designation: housing, shaft, bearing, bolt, nut, washer.
Assign quantities: housing 1, shaft 1, bearing 2, bolt 4, nut 4, washer 8.
Add the quantities to find the total pieces.

blocks.answer: The BOM has 6 lines and 20 individual pieces.

blocks.markdown: A BOM tells you what is in the assembly; **revision control** tells you which version of the information you are looking at. A released drawing is a legal and manufacturing instruction. When it must change (a hole moved, a tolerance tightened) you do not simply overwrite it. You raise the **issue number** or revision letter (A, B, C, or 1, 2, 3) and record the change in the **revision table**, normally placed near the title block: revision letter, description of change, date, and the person who made and approved it.

blocks.title: Why the revision table exists
blocks.text: Two people holding different copies can build different parts from the same drawing number. The issue letter and the revision table make the difference visible and traceable, so a supplier working to issue B can be told it is obsolete when issue C is released.

blocks.title: Recording a change
blocks.prompt: A flange drawing is at issue B. The 12 mm hole diameter is changed to 13 mm to suit a larger bolt, and the surface finish note is deleted. Write the revision entry and say what the issue letter becomes.

steps.text: A change to a released drawing is made, so the issue must advance one step: B to C.
Describe each change precisely in the revision table: hole diameter increased from 12 mm to 13 mm; surface finish note removed.
Add the date and the initials of originator and approver, and update the issue field in the title block to match.

blocks.answer: New issue C; revision row: C, hole dia 12 changed to 13, finish note deleted, date, originator, approver.

blocks.markdown: Before a drawing package is released to manufacture, it should be **checked for completeness**: every part on the assembly has a part drawing or standard designation; the BOM and balloons agree; each part drawing has a fully populated title block with material and tolerance; dimensions are complete and not duplicated; and the issue letter agrees with the revision table.

items: Every balloon number appears in the BOM and vice versa.
Every BOM line has a part drawing or a standard designation.
Quantities are consistent with the assembly view.
Title block: part number, title, material, scale, general tolerance, issue.
Revision table matches the issue letter on every sheet.

blocks.title: Typical errors
blocks.text: Missing standard parts (washers, O-rings), a balloon with no BOM line, and an issue letter that does not match the revision table are the classic mistakes an examiner asks you to find.

points: A BOM lists each distinct part once with a quantity per assembly; balloons link the drawing to the list.
The revision table and issue letter record every change to a released drawing so that obsolete copies can be identified.
A completeness check cross-references balloons, BOM, part drawings, title blocks and revisions before release.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the item number in a BOM line?

options.text: It gives the cost of the part
It links the line to the balloon on the assembly view
It states the material
It shows the issue letter

questions.correctOptionText: It links the line to the balloon on the assembly view

distractorRationale.a: Cost is not an item number function.
distractorRationale.d: Issue is in the title block or revision table.

questions.explanation: Item numbers are the key between the picture and the list. Cost, material and issue are separate fields.

questions.stem: What does a revision table record?

options.text: The tolerance on each dimension
The history of changes made to a released drawing
The materials used in the assembly
The list of standard fasteners

questions.correctOptionText: The history of changes made to a released drawing

distractorRationale.a: Tolerances sit on the views or in the title block.
distractorRationale.c: This is the BOM material column.
distractorRationale.d: This is part of the BOM.

questions.explanation: It is the log of what changed, when and who approved, paired with the issue letter. The other items belong elsewhere on the drawing.

questions.stem: A gear pump assembly contains one body, one cover, two gears, two shafts, six screws, two dowel pins and one O-ring. Give the total number of individual pieces per assembly (the sum of the BOM quantities).
questions.explanation: Sum: 1 + 1 + 2 + 2 + 6 + 2 + 1 = 15 pieces per assembly. Note that the BOM would have 7 lines, not 15, because identical parts share a line.

questions.stem: Each gear pump needs six M6 screws. A batch of 40 pumps is planned and stores wants 10 spare screws. How many screws should be ordered?
questions.explanation: Needed for the batch is 40 x 6 = 240; adding 10 spares gives 250. The per-assembly quantity in the BOM is the multiplier for ordering.

questions.stem: A part drawing is released unchanged except that the hole diameter was edited from 12 mm to 13 mm. Which action is correct?

options.text: Overwrite the dimension and keep the old issue letter
Advance the issue letter and add a revision table entry
Delete the old drawing from the record
Change the part number to a new number only

questions.correctOptionText: Advance the issue letter and add a revision table entry

distractorRationale.a: Others may be working to the old size.
distractorRationale.d: The part number identifies the part, not the version.

questions.explanation: A change to a released drawing needs a new issue and a recorded entry so everyone can tell versions apart. Silent overwrite defeats traceability.

questions.stem: A supplier has a purchase order that cites the drawing at issue B. Issue C has since been released with a larger hole. What is the most likely outcome?

options.text: The part is made to issue C anyway
The part is made to the superseded issue B and may be wrong
The supplier rejects the order automatically
The part cannot be made at all

questions.correctOptionText: The part is made to the superseded issue B and may be wrong
questions.explanation: The order controls which version the supplier uses, so it makes the part to B. This is why the issue letter is carried on the PO and the revision table is checked.

questions.stem: A drawing package has these defects: balloon 7 does not appear in the BOM; the BOM lists a washer that is not shown on the assembly; the revision table shows issue D but the title block says issue C. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Only the issue mismatch matters
All three are completeness defects and the package should not be released
None of them matter if the part drawings are fine
Only the missing BOM line matters

questions.correctOptionText: All three are completeness defects and the package should not be released
questions.explanation: Balloon, BOM and revision data must agree. Any one of them can cause a wrong part to be bought or made, so release should wait.

questions.stem: Explain how balloons, item numbers and the BOM work together on an assembly drawing, and why an identical part appearing four times gets one BOM line.
markingGuide: Each part on the assembly view has a balloon with an item number
The item number matches one line in the BOM
The BOM line gives part number, description, quantity, material
Identical parts share a line with qty 4, avoiding duplicate lines
Different parts never share a line even if similar
questions.explanation: Balloons key the picture to the list. A single line with a quantity is clearer and reduces counting mistakes than four repeated lines.

questions.stem: List five checks you would make on a drawing package before release to manufacture and say what failure each check prevents.
markingGuide: Balloons match BOM lines: prevents missing or extra parts
Every BOM line has a drawing or standard designation: prevents unobtainable items
Title blocks complete with material, tolerance, scale: prevents wrong material or scale
Dimensions complete without duplication: prevents ambiguous size
Issue letter agrees with the revision table: prevents obsolete versions
questions.explanation: A good answer pairs each check with a concrete failure it prevents, such as a missing part or an obsolete copy being built. Each point in the marking guide earns credit, so state every point explicitly and give its reason.

questions.stem: The issue number must be advanced whenever a released drawing is altered.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Every alteration to a released drawing needs a new issue and a revision entry. Otherwise two versions share one identity.
